summary: Eicher Motors designs and builds Royal Enfield motorcycles, such as the Classic 350, Hunter 350 and Himalayan, and sells them with spare parts, servicing, helmets and riding clothes in India and abroad.
description: Royal Enfield has made motorcycles since 1901 and specialises in middleweight bikes, with engines from 250cc to 750cc. Eicher buys parts from suppliers and assembles the bikes in three factories near Chennai. Dealers sell them from more than 2,074 stores across India and about 1,212 stores in other countries, and the same stores sell spare parts, accessories and service. Eicher also owns part of a separate joint company with Sweden’s Volvo Group, VECV (VE Commercial Vehicles), which makes Eicher trucks and buses.
money: Eicher earns most of its income by selling motorcycles to its dealers and overseas distributors, who then sell to riders. It also earns from spare parts, servicing, accessories and riding clothes. Its main costs are steel, aluminium and other parts, factory workers, marketing and building factories. For VECV, it counts only its share of that company’s profit, not its sales. A dealer’s payment is revenue, not profit.
customers: Riders choose the bike, but Eicher’s direct customers are the dealers it bills and, abroad, distributors and its own overseas companies. Royal Enfield describes its Indian buyers as business owners, farmers, students, government employees and other professionals. On the 29 July 2026 earnings call, its managing director estimated that most buyers are upgrading from another motorcycle and about a quarter are buying their first. Brazil is its biggest market outside India.
drivers: How many motorcycles it sells in India and abroad, the price it can charge compared with steel, aluminium and parts costs, and how much extra riders spend on accessories, parts and servicing.

groups.title: 350cc motorcycles
groups.examples: The Classic 350, Bullet 350, Hunter 350, Meteor 350 and Goan Classic 350.
groups.explanation: Royal Enfield’s best-selling bikes, with a single-cylinder engine of about 350 cubic centimetres. They are bought for daily riding and weekend trips, and many buyers are moving up from a smaller motorcycle.

groups.title: Bigger bikes: 450cc and 650cc
groups.examples: The Himalayan 450, Guerrilla 450, Interceptor 650, Classic 650, Bullet 650, Super Meteor 650, Shotgun 650 and Bear 650.
groups.explanation: More powerful and more expensive motorcycles for touring, rough roads or a sportier ride. Managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that sales of these had returned to their level before a tax change made them dearer.

groups.title: Electric motorcycles
groups.examples: The Flying Flea C6, first sold in Bengaluru from June 2026.
groups.explanation: Royal Enfield’s first battery-powered motorcycle, sold under a separate brand for city riding. It is being launched one city at a time, so sales are small for now.

groups.title: Parts, servicing, accessories and clothing
groups.examples: A service at a Royal Enfield workshop, replacement parts, a luggage rack, a helmet or a riding jacket.
groups.explanation: Money earned after the sale. Managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that these allied businesses were about 15% of revenue and that most buyers add accessories.

groups.title: Trucks and buses through VECV
groups.examples: Eicher trucks and buses, Volvo buses, and Volvo trucks sold in India.
groups.explanation: Made and sold by VE Commercial Vehicles, a joint company with the Volvo Group. Its sales are not added to Eicher’s revenue; Eicher records its share of VECV’s profit.

basics.title: What does 350cc mean?
basics.text: It is the size of the engine, measured in cubic centimetres (cc), the space inside the engine where fuel burns. A bigger number usually means more power and a higher price. Royal Enfield calls bikes from 250cc to 750cc middleweight.

basics.title: What is the difference between wholesale and retail sales?
basics.text: A wholesale sale is when Eicher bills a dealer for a bike. A retail sale is when the dealer sells it to a rider. Eicher’s revenue comes from billing dealers, so bikes waiting in dealers’ stores have already been sold as far as Eicher is concerned.

basics.title: What is a joint venture, and why is VECV counted differently?
basics.text: A joint venture is a company owned by two partners who share control. VECV is shared with Volvo, so Eicher does not add VECV’s sales to its own. It adds only its share of VECV’s profit, as a single line.

basics.title: What is kit assembly abroad?
basics.text: CKD (completely knocked down) assembly means bikes are shipped abroad as kits of parts and put together in a local plant. Royal Enfield has seven such plants, including two in Brazil.

steps.title: Design and buy parts
steps.text: Engineers in technical centres in the UK and Chennai design each bike. Eicher buys steel, aluminium and many finished parts from suppliers.

steps.title: Build the bikes
steps.text: Workers assemble the motorcycles in three factories near Chennai, running three shifts at busy times. Kits for some countries are sent abroad for local assembly.

steps.title: Bill the dealer
steps.text: Finished bikes go to depots and then to dealers, or straight to dealers. Eicher bills the dealer, and that bill is Eicher’s revenue.

steps.title: The dealer sells to a rider
steps.text: The rider pays the dealer. Many add accessories and riding gear from Royal Enfield at the same time.

steps.title: Years of servicing and parts
steps.text: The rider returns for servicing and replacement parts, which bring Eicher income long after the sale. Revenue (what dealers are billed), profit (what is left after costs) and cash collected are different things.

specifics.title: One brand does most of the work
specifics.text: Making motorcycles is 85.5% of the company’s own turnover, by its sustainability report. Eicher’s results therefore rise and fall mainly with Royal Enfield’s bike sales.

specifics.title: Prices follow metal costs with a delay
specifics.text: Each bike is built from steel, aluminium and many bought-in parts. Eicher says it manages these costs through other suppliers, redesigning parts to cost less and price changes, which come after costs move.

specifics.title: Kits assembled abroad
specifics.text: Royal Enfield ships some bikes as kits of parts to seven local assembly plants in Bangladesh, Nepal, Brazil (two), Thailand, Argentina and Colombia, and sells through about 1,212 stores outside India.

specifics.title: The truck business is outside revenue
specifics.text: VECV is a large company in its own right, but because it is a joint venture with Volvo, Eicher’s revenue does not include it. Compare Eicher’s profit with and without its share of VECV’s profit.

watch: Are 350cc sales still growing after the tax change?
The 350cc bikes are most of Royal Enfield’s volume, and the GST change of 2025–26 taxes them less than bigger bikes.
Compare monthly sales releases and each quarter’s press release, split into 350cc and bigger bikes, against the same months a year earlier.
Is the gross margin, what is left of each sale after paying for materials and parts, holding up?
If parts and metals cost more and prices do not rise as much, each bike earns less.
Read the earnings call for comments on commodity costs and price increases, and compare raw material cost with revenue in the quarterly results.
Is the new capacity arriving on time?
Managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that dealers held only about 10 to 12 days of stock. Too little capacity means lost sales; too much means idle factories.
Follow updates on the Cheyyar expansion and the planned Tada factory in quarterly releases and calls, and compare production with sales.
How much does VECV add to profit?
The share of VECV’s profit is added to Eicher’s profit but none of its sales are in revenue, which can make profit margins look higher.
Find the line for share of profit from the joint venture in the consolidated results, and read VECV’s own figures in the press release.
Will the electric Flying Flea sell beyond Bengaluru?
Electric bikes are a new product that costs money to develop and launch before it earns.
Track the number of cities, stores and deliveries mentioned in each quarterly call and press release.
risks: Managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that commodity inflation cut the margin and that price increases covered only part of it. Raising prices too far could slow sales.
Eicher’s managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that it chose not to shrink its 450cc and 650cc engines to get a lower GST rate, so those bikes stay costlier for buyers than 350cc models.
Supply and labour problems stop the factories

Managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that in April to June 2026 Eicher dealt with a gas shortage, a shortage of workers and scarce key materials. Every lost day of production is a lost sale when dealer stocks are thin.
Weak demand in some overseas markets
Managers described the USA on the 29 July 2026 call as very slow and said many European dealers and distributors were under business pressure, which limits growth abroad.
Eicher has approved expansion near Chennai and a new factory in Andhra Pradesh. If demand slows, it still carries the cost of the extra capacity.
context: April to June 2026: record sales and a new factory plan

On 29 July 2026 Eicher said Royal Enfield sold 332,940 motorcycles in April to June 2026, its highest ever, against 261,326 in the same quarter a year earlier, a rise of 27%. It began delivering its first electric motorcycle, the Flying Flea C6, in Bengaluru. Its board approved the first phase of a new factory in Tada, Andhra Pradesh, expected to be completed in 2029–30, subject to market conditions. This is a plan, not built capacity. Results for July to September 2026 were due on 13 November 2026.

financialNotes.title: Read Eicher’s numbers with VECV in mind
financialNotes.text: Eicher’s consolidated revenue, meaning Eicher and its subsidiaries together, is mostly Royal Enfield. VE Commercial Vehicles (VECV) reports its own revenue, which is not included; Eicher adds only its share of VECV’s profit. In the year to 31 March 2026 (audited), revenue from operations was ₹23,408 crore, about 24% more than a year earlier, and profit after tax (PAT, what is left after all costs and tax) was ₹5,515 crore. That profit includes ₹798 crore as Eicher’s share of VECV’s profit and is after a one-off ₹55.5 crore charge for the estimated cost of India’s new labour laws (the Labour Codes). Eicher also earned ₹1,487 crore of other income, mostly from its investments, which is not counted as revenue.

stepsTitle: From a factory near Chennai to a rider.

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: Eicher designs and builds Royal Enfield motorcycles near Chennai and sells them, along with parts, servicing and riding gear. It also part-owns a truck and bus maker.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Dealers and overseas distributors pay Eicher for the motorcycles, then sell them to riders. Riders pay for parts, accessories and servicing at the same stores.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: Mainly from selling motorcycles. Spare parts, servicing, accessories and clothing add more. From the truck business it records only its share of profit.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Metals and bought-in parts, factory workers, marketing, new motorcycle designs and new factory space.

helps.title: An old brand with a loyal following
helps.text: Royal Enfield is the oldest motorcycle brand still in production and runs rides and festivals such as Motoverse and the Himalayan Odyssey. Riders who identify with the brand come back for the next bike, accessories and events.

helps.title: Income that continues after the sale
helps.text: Every bike sold needs servicing and parts for years, and many riders add accessories and riding gear. This income comes from people who already own a Royal Enfield, so it does not depend only on new sales.

helps.title: A wide dealer network at home and abroad
helps.text: Royal Enfield sells through more than 2,074 stores in India and about 1,212 stores in over 80 countries, so new models reach buyers quickly.

hurts.title: Metal and parts costs can jump
hurts.text: Eicher’s sustainability report says a weak supply chain can cause production disruptions and profit pressure. When metals get dearer, prices rise only later; managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that input costs had risen sharply that quarter.

hurts.title: Tax rules by engine size
hurts.text: India taxes smaller bikes at a lower GST rate than bigger ones. Managers said on the 29 July 2026 call that Eicher chose not to shrink its 450cc and 650cc engines to qualify, so those bikes stay dearer for buyers.

hurts.title: Factories depend on people and suppliers
hurts.text: Eicher’s sustainability report describes its work as labour-intensive. A shortage of workers, gas or parts stops the lines, and every lost day is a lost sale when dealers hold little stock.

hurts.title: Riders’ tastes and technology can change
hurts.text: Eicher’s sustainability report warns that new technology and changing customer expectations may make existing products less relevant. Its first electric bike, the Flying Flea C6, is still being launched one city at a time.
